findings.title: Tray "Settings" opens a second dialog when one is already open on the hidden window
findings.body: The window now stays alive when hidden, so a dialog stays open after it is hidden to the tray. Issue #467 is exactly that case. Sequence: open Settings, hide to tray, then pick tray → Settings. The window is shown and `ShowSettingsCommand.Execute(null)` runs again. CommunityToolkit's `Execute` does not check `CanExecute`, so a second dialog is pushed onto a `DialogHost` that is already open. That usually throws ("DialogHost is already open"). The fire-and-forget `Execute` call then passes the exception to the dispatcher, which can crash the app. Before this change the window was rebuilt each time, so this could not happen. Fix: skip the call when the command cannot run or a dialog is already open, for example `if (_mainViewModel.ShowSettingsCommand.CanExecute(null)) ...`, or just show the window when a dialog is already open.

held.title: Start-hidden check runs on every Loaded, not only the first
held.body: `Window_OnLoaded` hides the window whenever `StartOptions.Current.IsInitiallyHidden` is set, and that option stays true for the whole process. If Avalonia raises `Loaded` again when a hidden window is shown (because the window is unloaded on `Hide`), then with `--start-hidden` every later `Toggle()`/`ShowActivateFocus()` from the tray or hotkey would hide the window right away, and the user could never open it. I could not confirm whether `Loaded` fires again after `Hide`/`Show` in the Avalonia version used here. The PR also says this was not tested. Fix: apply the hide only once, for example with a `_hasHandledStartup` flag or by unsubscribing the handler after its first run.
